title: Route customer bug reports from Slack to your developers
summary: A founder at Kendo used Claude Code to build a Slack bot that scans enterprise customer channels several times a day and forwards likely bugs to a developer channel.
agent_role: Claude Code wrote the bot; the bot scans customer channels, spots likely bugs, reposts them to an escalations channel and tags the right developers. The founder directed the build.
outcome: Author reports developers now check one channel instead of many, and the build took only a few minutes without pulling engineers off the product.
what_they_did: A founder at Kendo noticed developers were being pulled into many shared customer Slack channels. He used Claude Code to build a Slack bot. It scans the customer channels several times a day for possible bugs or technical issues. It forwards them to one escalations channel and tags the relevant developers.
how_it_went: The author says developers now have one place to see what needs attention. He says it took a few minutes and needed no engineer's time.
prompt: Help me build a Slack bot for my team. Several times a day it should read new messages in these customer channels: [list of channels]. Flag any message that looks like a bug report or technical problem. Repost each flagged message, with a link to the original, into [escalations channel] and tag the right person based on this list: [topic → developer]. First show me your plan, the permissions the bot needs, and a few sample flags from recent messages. Wait for my approval before installing it or posting anything.

curation.rationale: A practical small-team workflow: a bot built with Claude Code scans customer Slack channels for bugs and routes them to developers. Clear and useful, but light on details and results.
